planning_constraints: Before Task dispatch, pin F3's actually integrated F1/F2 source revisions and concrete budget, provider receipt, owner routing, delivery and Watchdog postcheck interfaces. Verify same-claim nested reservation and conservative unavailable-usage charging against delivered source/tests. Preserve one Task-owned incident budget in tracking-trunk executions.json under the lifecycle lock. Missing integration evidence needs a supported delivery handoff, not another ledger or another team's worktree edit.

Replace F3's TBD schemas/APIs and Start-to-End flow through Cascade read_doc/write_doc before feature sign-off. Specify the startup receipt, authoritative expected artifact/review input, independent comparison result, capability generation and typed waiting/refusal outcomes. Name persistence, producer, consumer, restart handling and trust boundaries. Copy applicable diagram rows into Task acceptance before dispatch.

Bind reviewed source, integrated commit, installed source/artifact identity, repository/environment identity, worker PID plus boot/start identity and capability generation separately. Capture identity from the runtime actually imported at process start; never recompute proof from a later mutable checkout HEAD or echo a caller-supplied expected SHA as observation. Define the receipt's covered modules/artifact and how mutable or mixed source is rejected. Missing, stale, dirty, wrong-checkout or unknown identity remains unresolved.

Independent postcheck must compare that loaded receipt to authoritative reviewed/integrated artifact evidence and observe the live process through supported health/UI entry points. A healthy endpoint, deployment receipt or valid loaded identity cannot waive unresolved product acceptance, unintegrated follow-up heads or the original delivery obligation. Retain separate reviewed, integrated, installed, loaded and verified states.

Use the supported launcher/worker drain and restart path and preserve queues, checkpoints, claims and usage. A lease timeout alone cannot reclaim a live owner. Demonstrate the repair of a recovery adapter through a supported bootstrap path independent of that failing adapter. When installation, credentials or operator authority is required, name the exact actor, action and evidence; do not hotpatch site-packages, dirty product trunk, call private repair functions or rewrite lifecycle state.

Compose F2's owner-tool journey with existing completed-parent/late-child repair, immutable source/target acceptance, parent integration and descendant-safe retirement. In split product/tracking repositories, retain the original incident budget and authoritative owner through cleanup and a fresh worker process. Independently compare board, execution, pending delivery, parent, review registry, loaded capability and historical incident after restart. Fix only integration gaps demonstrated by this journey; do not duplicate late-child machinery.

Crash immediately after leased push and before its completion receipt; reconcile the real remote effect before replay. Count publication, worker/Task/repair/message effects independently under repeat sweeps and competing callers. Live owners, changed target/policy, unavailable authoritative evidence and unfinished acceptance remain pending. Resolve through the production independent Watchdog verification route, never a raw success setter.

The harness must start a real worker from a pinned reviewed repair in an isolated prepared workspace, use real temporary repositories/bare remote, validators, durable stores, queues/checkpoints and scoped production tools. Script only external paid-provider/forge transports. Include stale old-worker after disk update, wrong checkout, missing/invalid receipt, dirty/unknown source and adapter stranded on a branch. Bound processes and retain failure diagnostics. This proves the isolated runtime contract, not production deployment.

Retain approved finite attempts, turn/process/runtime/elapsed bounds and original lineage across restart/bootstrap/parent escalation. No source change, new process, capability generation or policy switch resets allowance. Unknown usage remains unknown and conservatively charged; use existing independent extension authority if the journey cannot fit. Keep assigned Codex and explicit descendant model/reasoning settings.

Supply F4 a concrete operational preflight artifact: exact target environment and product/tracking/runtime roots, reviewed/integrated artifact, permitted failure injection, supported entry points, independent operator/install/credential authority, command/budget, rollback/cleanup and expected independent postcheck evidence. Unknown target or missing authority is an explicit named prerequisite; do not invent approval or use the local dependency manifest as deployment permission. Update declarations through the owning tools before using new software or another environment.

F3 owns loaded-runtime/bootstrap and cross-stage delivery proof. F2 owns reconciliation of its final acceptance evidence and Task 001 record gap; F4 owns broad adversarial CI, measured budget feasibility and the authorized controlled supervisor exercise. Do not silently absorb those scopes or declare the epic complete. Request an epic amendment if parent policy, authority, ownership or sequencing must change.
